answer: Each calf is punched with an ear tag at birth and the number is filed with the cattle clerk, and no beast may be sold unless its tag matches the file. A velvet calf tagged with a copied punch fails the book: the terrace of the herd must carry tags the clerk issued, and a copied tag hangs crooked in the ear. Forging the herd means keeping cattle for a year, punching 120 tags and paying 14,800, while the copper number in the clerk's file is read at every sale, so a beast whose tag was never filed is driven back to the hill.
